title: Resources & Community
text: Badger Biodata works closely alongside BRUG to share resources and collaborate. One of the responsibilities of Badger Biodata is to participate in BRUG’s meetings and contributing to BRUG’s website.

title: Resources & Community
text:
Available Databases

NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus
Database of transciptomic datasets. These datasets explore gene expression for varying conditions and diseases. Great for comparing genes and finding what is driving diseases.


IPUMS USA
IPUMS is the world’s largest database for census and survey data. Much of the data can be used to analyze social and economic change.


Environmental Data Initiative
The EDI Data Portal holds ecological data packages. It was jointly created by the University of Wisconsin and the University of New Mexico. Although it has data from all over the globe, it is a great place to find ecological data for Wisconsin.


National Ecological Observatory Network (NEON)
Has ecoclimatic and organismal sampling data from the Midwest and Great Lakes region.

title: Welcome!
text:
Badger Biodata Initiative




Coding With Real Biology.

The Badger Biodata Mission
We serve to promote a space on campus for learning, creating, and innovating with  biological data programming. Our mission is to give each member the opportunity to produce real collaborative projects using industry tools and methods.


The Value We Bring
 Collaboration is the foundation of our organization. We work alongside labs, student organizations, and other local groups whom have real biological data. Our members work in development teams to produce projects with those datasets, which can create real impact for conservation and efforts and research on campus.


Our Space On Campus
We foster a tight-knit community environment focused on learning through practice. No member has to be an expert, everyone is encouraged to join and learn.



Connecting with Us

Collaborators
For labs, student clubs, and speakers, please reach out to our club email: badgerbiodata@gmail.com


For those interested in membership
We are excited to see you! Fill out our Interested Membership Form, Membership is processed with 2 weeks. Watch your inbox for updates.


Current members
Utilize our Discord server, or contact a leader.

title: Member Projects
text:
Have a project idea? Fill out the Request Project Idea Form to have your idea listed below!



CNN Model Analyzing non-coding DNA for Cancer
Currently Ongoing Python Machine Learning
Using Supervised training for a CNN to analyze large DNA datasets, specifically the non-coding DNA sequences, to discover possible patterns that result in Melanomia cancer.

  GitHub Repository 
Author(s): Jayden Merrick






Madison Lakeshore Preserve Biodiversity Trends Map
Project Idea Statistical Trends Mapping
Lakeshore preserve plant data, collect by a local organization, that is mapped to display possible future trends for the biodiversity of the area.






UW Arboretum Invasive Species Mapping
Project Idea Mapping
Uses INaturalist data and API to map out the invasive Buckthorn and Garlic Mustard with a spatial distribution model. This can directly act as actionable conservation data.






Species Nucleotide Count Comparisons
Project Idea R
Counting and plotting the percentages of each nucleotide of differing species using a DNA FASTA file. Uses Chargaff’s rules to justify counting two bases. Data can be from Ensembl.






Comparative Genomics of Disease Resistance (NLR) Genes
Project Idea R
Catalog and compare Nucleotide-Binding Leucine-Rich Repeat (NLR) immune receptor genes across wild and domesticated plant relatives. Data can be sources from NCBI GenBank genome assemblies.
